skill.name: security-guardian
skill.description: Application security guidance for reviewing code, identifying common vulnerabilities, and planning secure remediation across OWASP, authentication, authorization, cryptography, secrets, APIs, and data protection.
skill.summary: Guided application-security reviews with OWASP-focused remediation advice.
skill.author: Bikach

security_audit.summary: All 400 static matches are false positives in a French-language application-security reference skill. The flagged strings appear in educational examples, checklists, or defensive detection guidance, and no executable code, credential access, or outbound network behavior was found. No prompt-injection text was found in the reviewed skill instructions.

remediation.issue: Static scanners interpret educational exploit examples as executable behavior.
remediation.suggestion: Keep dangerous examples clearly labeled as unsafe and pair each one with a safe alternative, as the current reference material generally does.

remediation.issue: The skill documentation permits Bash for read-oriented security review.
remediation.suggestion: State that commands must be scoped to authorized repositories and should avoid destructive or network-active actions unless the user explicitly authorizes them.

content.value_statement: Security reviews can miss issues across authentication, input handling, APIs, and secrets. This skill provides structured guidance, checklists, and remediation patterns for application-security work.
actual_capabilities: Reviews source code for common application-security weaknesses.
Guides assessment of authentication, authorization, sessions, OAuth, and MFA.
Explains defensive patterns for injection, XSS, CSRF, SSRF, XXE, and path traversal.
Provides checklists for secrets, cryptography, logging, APIs, and data protection.
Organizes findings by severity with remediation-oriented guidance.
limitations: It does not replace a penetration test or independent security assessment.
It cannot prove that an application is secure without complete code and deployment context.
It does not automatically run vulnerability scanners or modify source files.
Recommendations require validation against the application architecture and threat model.

use_cases.title: Review a pull request
use_cases.description: Identify likely security weaknesses in a focused code change and propose practical remediation.

use_cases.title: Design a sensitive feature
use_cases.description: Plan controls for login, payments, user data, APIs, or file uploads before implementation.

use_cases.title: Prepare a security checklist
use_cases.description: Create a structured review plan for OWASP risks, secrets, logging, and deployment controls.

prompt_templates.title: Start a basic review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this code for common application-security issues. List findings by severity and explain the safest next step.

prompt_templates.title: Review authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this authentication flow for password, session, JWT, MFA, and authorization weaknesses. Provide prioritized remediation.

prompt_templates.title: Assess an API change
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this API change for input validation, CORS, rate limiting, SSRF, authorization, and sensitive-data exposure. Include test cases to verify fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a threat-informed plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this architecture and data flow to produce a threat-informed security review. Cover trust boundaries, abuse cases, compensating controls, and a remediation order.

output: High: Validate file type from content, not the submitted filename.
High: Generate server-side names and store uploads outside the web root.
Next step: Add size limits, authorization checks, and malware scanning where appropriate.
High: Verify signatures with an explicit allowlist of accepted algorithms.
Medium: Rotate refresh tokens and revoke compromised sessions.
Positive: Use short-lived access tokens and secure cookie settings.

best_practices: Provide relevant code, configuration, data flows, and deployment assumptions.
Confirm findings with tests and manual review before treating them as production defects.
Prioritize critical trust-boundary and data-exposure issues before hardening work.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a checklist-only review as a complete security assessment.
Do not apply remediation blindly without considering application behavior and compatibility.
Do not share real secrets, private keys, or production credentials in prompts.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It guides application-security reviews for common web risks, identity controls, APIs, secrets, cryptography, logging, and data protection.

faq.question: Does it execute security tests?
faq.answer: No. It provides review guidance and may suggest validation steps, but it does not replace authorized testing tools.

faq.question: Can it review authentication code?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for passwords, sessions, JWTs, OAuth, MFA, and authorization patterns.

faq.question: Does it support OWASP Top 10 reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. The reference material includes OWASP-oriented checklists and common vulnerability guidance.

faq.question: Should I provide production secrets?
faq.answer: No. Remove or redact secrets, private keys, tokens, and personal data before sharing code.

faq.question: Is its output a security certification?
faq.answer: No. Validate recommendations with your security process and obtain independent review for high-impact systems.
